speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you are experiencing hand tremors and memory problems. To understand what's happening, how long have these symptoms been present, and are there any family members with similar conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history; the progressive nature of the tremor starting in one hand is concerning. Have you noticed any stiffness or slowness in his movements, and has he experienced any falls or changes in his handwriting? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain, Thyroid_Function_Test.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: No acute abnormalities. Mild age-appropriate cerebral atrophy. Thyroid Function Tests: TSH 2.5 mIU/L, Free_T4 1.2 ng/dL.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms of resting tremor, soft speech, reduced facial expressions, and financial mismanagement are highly characteristic of Parkinson's disease, not iron deficiency anemia. Can you describe the quality of his handwriting and whether he has experienced any stiffness or slowness in his movements?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: No acute abnormalities. Mild age-appropriate cerebral atrophy.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease. The clinical presentation of asymmetric resting tremor, bradykinesia (implied by stiffness/slowness), masked facies, and cognitive decline, combined with the exclusion of acute structural causes on MRI, strongly supports this diagnosis.
